import pandas as pd,numpy as np

import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from scipy.signal import find_peaks,savgol_filter
d=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv');x=d.shift_cm1.values;y=d.intensity.values
s=savgol_filter(y,9,2)
for lo in range(60,1100,40):
  m=(x>=lo)&(x<lo+40);print(lo,round(s[m].mean()),round(y[m].max()))

for i,q in zip(p,pr['prominences']):print(round(x[i],1),round(s[i]),round(q))
"

candidates.evidence: Three sharp lines at 155.7, 299.3 and 354.1 cm-1 with nothing above ~400 cm-1 match a heavy-metal oxychloride of the FeOCl type (Pmmn). I did not check this against a reference spectrum. The set does not match BiOCl, SnS2 or the In2Se3 phases, so the identification is tentative.
The 156 cm-1 line is near the A1g mode at about 145 cm-1. But BiOCl also shows Eg at about 200 cm-1 and B1g/Eg at about 397 cm-1, and neither is seen here.

candidates.material: Other FeOCl-type MOCl (e.g. FeOCl, TiOCl, CrOCl)
candidates.evidence: The structure type fits the pattern of a few low-frequency lines. The mode energies reported for these compounds differ from those seen here.
Their main lines are near 90-110 and 180-230 cm-1, which does not fit 156 and 354 cm-1.

peaks.assignment: Lowest-frequency, strongest mode; probably a heavy-atom (In-Cl) vibration, totally symmetric (Ag)
peaks.source: Position and FWHM measured from a Lorentzian fit. The mode symmetry is inferred by analogy with FeOCl-type (Pmmn) oxychlorides. I did not check it against a reference.

peaks.assignment: Weak mid-frequency mode; probably an In-O stretching/bending vibration
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit; weak, about 1000 counts above background and about 3 times the noise. The assignment is not verified.

peaks.assignment: Higher-frequency mode; probably an In-O stretching vibration
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit. The mode type is inferred from the frequency. The material was not confirmed.

properties.source: The lines are narrow, with FWHM of 5-9 cm-1, and no broad disorder band appears.

artifacts.type: cosmic-ray spike (single point, ~9200 counts against a ~1500 background)
sloping photoluminescence-like background (decreasing from ~2900 to ~1000 counts across the range)

citations: FeOCl-type MOCl structure (Pmmn) – general knowledge; no reference spectrum was checked against the data
BiOCl Raman: A1g about 145 cm-1, Eg about 200 cm-1, B1g/Eg about 397 cm-1 (recalled from memory, not re-checked)
limits: The identification is tentative. I did not check the spectrum against a reference InOCl Raman spectrum, and I am not sure of the published mode positions.
The data are single-polarization with no angle resolution and no substrate, so the mode symmetries and polarization patterns cannot be assigned.
The 299 cm-1 peak is weak, only about 3 times the noise, and should be treated as probable rather than certain.
I did not detect a Si substrate line at 520.7 cm-1, and the spectral range is only about 60-1100 cm-1. Nothing above 1100 cm-1 was examined.
The single-point spike at 897.5 cm-1 was rejected as a cosmic ray. Neighbouring points are at background, and a real Raman line would span several points.

The isostructural oxychlorides (FeOCl, TiOCl, CrOCl) and BiOCl were considered and mostly ruled out by the peak positions. The data cannot exclude an unlisted compound with a similar low-frequency spectrum.
The layer number, strain and doping cannot be determined from this spectrum.
